title.en: Multi-Region: Global Tables, S3 Replication, and Route 53

sources.title: How DynamoDB global tables work
supports: A global table has two or more replicas in different Regions, one per Region, all with the same table name and key schema
The default consistency mode is multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC), and the mode cannot be changed after creation
In MREC, item changes are replicated asynchronously, typically within a second or less
In MREC, simultaneous changes to one item in several Regions are resolved by the latest internal timestamp per item (last writer wins)
In MREC, a strongly consistent read may return stale data if the item was last updated in another Region, and a conditional write evaluates its condition against the item's version in the Region
In MRSC, a change is replicated synchronously to at least one other Region before the write returns, and conditional writes evaluate against the latest version
An MRSC global table spans exactly three Regions: three replicas, or two replicas and a witness that cannot be read or written
A write to an item being modified in another Region fails with ReplicatedWriteConflictException in MRSC and can be retried
TTL and local secondary indexes are not supported in MRSC; transactions are not supported in MRSC and are atomic only within one Region in MREC
MREC has an RPO equal to the replication delay; MRSC supports an RPO of zero
MREC publishes the ReplicationLatency metric per source and destination Region pair; MRSC does not
Global tables have a 99.999% availability SLA, single-Region tables 99.99%
AWS FIS can pause replication to and from a replica to simulate Region isolation
MRSC is available in Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka among other Regions
sources.note: This page says an MRSC table can combine any three of the listed Regions; the design guide (mr-dynamodb-global-tables-design) lists Region sets that cannot be mixed. Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka are in one set either way.

sources.title: Using DynamoDB global tables
supports: DynamoDB has no global endpoint: every request goes to a Regional endpoint and reaches the replica in that Region
MREC write conflicts are not recorded in CloudWatch or CloudTrail
There is no SLA on ReplicationLatency; a new item usually reaches all replicas within a second
Each item carries a private last-write timestamp, and an incoming replicated item is applied only if its timestamp is greater
Items are replicated individually, and the order of writes in a remote Region may differ from the source Region
The local Region accepts writes while another Region is offline, and pending replication is retried when it returns
With MRSC, a Region accepts reads and writes only while a second Region (replica or witness) is reachable; otherwise it serves eventually consistent reads only
MRSC Region sets: Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka form the AP set, and a table cannot span sets
MRSC was introduced in June 2025

sources.title: Write modes with DynamoDB global tables
supports: Global tables are always active-active at the table level; treating one as active-passive is done by routing writes outside DynamoDB
Writing to one Region avoids conflicts in MREC and is what conditional expressions and transactions need
Writing to any Region suits MRSC tables, and MREC tables whose writes are idempotent assignments

sources.title: Evacuation processes
supports: Moving the write Region of an MREC table means pausing writes, waiting for replication, then resuming in the new Region
No metric says with certainty that replication has completed; waiting ten times the recent maximum ReplicationLatency is given as typically sufficient for a healthy Region
When an MREC Region goes offline, its unreplicated writes are held and propagated after it returns, and a later update in the other Region suppresses them under last writer wins

sources.title: Understanding Amazon DynamoDB billing for global tables
supports: A write to a global table is billed as one replicated write request unit per replica table, in each replica's Region
Replicated write units are priced the same as single-Region write units
DynamoDB does not charge cross-Region data transfer for replication between the Regions of a global table
A witness incurs no replicated write, storage or transfer cost

sources.title: Best practices for global tables
supports: CloudFormation cannot coordinate a global table across stacks: all replicas should be defined in one Region's stack
Changing a resource's type from AWS::DynamoDB::Table to AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable may delete the table
Deletion protection is enabled per replica
Point-in-time recovery on one replica may be enough for disaster recovery objectives

sources.title: Replicating objects within and across Regions
supports: S3 replication copies objects asynchronously
Replicas retain metadata such as the original creation time and version ID
Two-way replication keeps buckets in two Regions in sync during a failover
Objects that existed before a rule was added are replicated with S3 Batch Replication, on demand

sources.title: What does Amazon S3 replicate?
supports: By default S3 replicates objects created after the replication configuration is added
With the current configuration format, delete markers are not replicated by default
A DELETE that names a version ID is not replicated to the destination
Objects that are themselves replicas created by another rule are not replicated
Delete markers added by a lifecycle action are not replicated

sources.title: Requirements and considerations for replication
supports: Both the source and the destination bucket must have versioning enabled

sources.title: Meeting compliance requirements with S3 Replication Time Control
supports: S3 RTC replicates most objects in seconds and 99.9 percent of objects within 15 minutes
S3 RTC rules publish replication metrics and can send events when an object misses the 15-minute threshold

sources.title: Replicating delete markers between buckets
supports: Without delete marker replication, a delete in the source adds a delete marker in the source only
Delete marker replication is not covered by the 15-minute S3 RTC SLA

sources.title: Getting replication status information
supports: A source object's replication status is PENDING, COMPLETED or FAILED, and a replica's is REPLICA

sources.title: Setting up permissions for live replication
supports: The replication role's actions: s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on the source bucket, s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication, s3:GetObjectVersionAcl and s3:GetObjectVersionTagging on its objects, and s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete and s3:ReplicateTags on the destination's objects

sources.title: Using S3 Replication metrics
supports: Replication metrics track bytes pending, operations pending, operations failed and replication latency
Replication metrics are billed at the rate of CloudWatch custom metrics

sources.title: Amazon S3 pricing (replication)
supports: Cross-Region replication is billed for destination storage, replication PUT requests at the destination Region's rate, and inter-Region data transfer out at the source Region's rate
S3 RTC adds a Replication Time Control data transfer charge and replication metrics charges
sources.note: Read as raw HTML; only the paragraph under Replication was used. Rates come from the Price List files.

sources.title: How Amazon Route 53 determines whether a health check is healthy
supports: Health checkers in several locations each send requests every 10 or 30 seconds and do not coordinate
A health check is healthy while more than 18% of health checkers report the endpoint healthy; the value may change
For HTTP and HTTPS, a checker must connect within four seconds and receive a 2xx or 3xx status within two seconds after connecting

sources.title: Values that you specify when you create or update health checks
supports: The failure threshold is the number of consecutive checks an endpoint must pass or fail to change status
With a 30-second interval an endpoint receives a request about every two seconds on average
HTTPS health checks carry an additional charge, and the protocol cannot be changed after creation

sources.title: Active-active and active-passive failover
supports: Active-passive failover uses the failover routing policy: the primary answers while healthy, the secondary when the primary is unhealthy
Active-active failover uses any other routing policy, and every healthy record can answer

sources.title: How Amazon Route 53 averts failover problems
supports: When all records are considered unhealthy, Route 53 reverts to considering all of them healthy

sources.title: Latency-based routing
supports: Latency records make Route 53 answer with the Region that gives the user the lowest latency, measured between users and AWS data centers

sources.title: Choosing between alias and non-alias records
supports: The TTL of an alias record that points to an AWS resource cannot be set; Route 53 uses the default TTL for the resource
sources.note: The page does not state the TTL used for an API Gateway domain name.

sources.title: Best practices for Amazon Route 53 DNS
supports: Route 53 health checks and ARC routing controls work in the data plane and do not depend on the control plane; failover should rely on them
The recommended range for TTL values is 60 to 172,800 seconds

sources.title: Amazon Route 53 pricing
supports: HTTPS, string matching, fast interval and latency measurement are optional health check features, each billed per month
Up to 50 health checks of AWS endpoints in or linked to the account are not charged
An AWS endpoint is a resource running in AWS in the same account as the health check or billed to it

sources.title: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
supports: Failover is PRIMARY on one record set and SECONDARY on the other, with SetIdentifier and HealthCheckId
A failover alias record set must set EvaluateTargetHealth to true

sources.title: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck HealthCheckConfig
supports: FailureThreshold defaults to three health checks

sources.title: Configure custom health checks for DNS failover for an API Gateway API
supports: With a custom domain name, a failover between Regions needs no change of endpoint in clients
With Evaluate Target Health alone, an alias record fails only when the API Gateway service is unavailable in the Region; custom health checks are for the API's own failures

sources.title: Set up a Regional custom domain name in API Gateway
supports: A Regional custom domain name needs an ACM certificate in the same Region as the API

sources.title: Amazon Cognito: Regional data considerations
supports: A user pool is created in one Region and stores user profile data only in that Region

sources.title: Replicate AWS Secrets Manager secrets across Regions
supports: A secret can be replicated to other Regions, and a replica can be promoted to a standalone secret

sources.title: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
supports: Parameter limits are stated per account and Region, and the page points to Secrets Manager for cross-Region replication
sources.note: Read while listing what stays in one Region; the chapter's text relies on the Secrets Manager page instead.

supports: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck, AWS::ApiGatewayV2::DomainName and AWS::ApiGatewayV2::ApiMapping are listed as supported

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: How Workers works
supports: Workers run on Cloudflare's global network, and a request is handled by the data center that receives it

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Global read replication
supports: Global read replication is marked Beta
Without read replication every query goes to one primary database instance in one location
Read replicas are asynchronously replicated, serve reads only, and may be arbitrarily out of date; all writes are forwarded to the primary
The Sessions API gives sequential consistency within a session

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Data location
supports: By default D1 creates the primary database instance close to where the create request was issued; a location hint or a jurisdiction can be given

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers KV: How KV works
supports: KV stores data in a small number of centralized data centers and caches it at the locations that read it
KV is eventually consistent: a change may take up to 60 seconds or more to be visible in other locations

sources.title: Cloudflare Durable Objects: Data location
supports: A Durable Object is created close to the first request for it and does not currently change location afterwards
A location hint or a jurisdiction can be given

sources.title: Cloudflare R2: Data location
supports: A bucket's location is chosen automatically near the create request unless a location hint or a jurisdiction is given

sources.title: Cloudflare R2: Durability
supports: R2 stores an object across several data centers within a geographic region
R2 has an availability SLA of 99.9%

sources.title: Vercel: Configuring regions for Vercel Functions
supports: Vercel Functions run in iad1 by default for new projects, and the region can be configured
Hobby is limited to a single region, Pro to 5 regions, Enterprise to all regions
functionFailoverRegions, the setting for failover regions, is available on Enterprise plans

glossary.ja: グローバルテーブル（global table）

definition.ja: DynamoDB のテーブルを複数のリージョンに置き、どのレプリカへの書き込みもほかのレプリカに届ける機能。レプリカはどれも読み書きできる。
definition.en: A DynamoDB table kept in several Regions, where a write to any replica is delivered to the others. Every replica accepts reads and writes.

definition.ja: グローバルテーブルの既定の整合性モード。書き込みは受けたリージョンで確定し、ほかのリージョンには後から届く。
definition.en: The default consistency mode of a global table: a write is final in the Region that took it and reaches the other Regions afterwards.

definition.ja: グローバルテーブルの整合性モードの 1 つ。書き込みは、ほかのリージョンの少なくとも 1 つに届いてから成功を返す。3 つのリージョンが要る。
definition.en: A consistency mode of a global table in which a write returns only after at least one other Region has it. It needs three Regions.

definition.ja: 同じアイテムへの書き込みが食い違ったとき、時刻の新しいほうを残し、古いほうを捨てる決め方。捨てられた書き込みは、どこにも記録されない。
definition.en: Resolving two conflicting writes to one item by keeping the one with the later timestamp and discarding the other. The discarded write is recorded nowhere.

definition.ja: MRSC のグローバルテーブルで、2 つのレプリカが合意するために使う 3 つ目のリージョン。読み書きはできない。
definition.en: The third Region of an MRSC global table, used so that two replicas can agree. It cannot be read or written.

glossary.ja: クロスリージョンレプリケーション（CRR）

definition.ja: S3 のバケットに書かれた新しいオブジェクトを、別のリージョンのバケットへ非同期にコピーする設定。
definition.en: An S3 configuration that asynchronously copies new objects written to a bucket into a bucket in another Region.

glossary.ja: フェイルオーバールーティング

definition.ja: Route 53 のルーティングポリシーの 1 つ。プライマリのレコードが正常なあいだはそれを返し、異常になるとセカンダリを返す。
definition.en: A Route 53 routing policy that answers with the primary record while it is healthy and with the secondary when it is not.

glossary.ja: レイテンシールーティング

definition.ja: Route 53 のルーティングポリシーの 1 つ。問い合わせた利用者から遅延のいちばん小さいリージョンのレコードを返す。
definition.en: A Route 53 routing policy that answers with the record of the Region that has the lowest latency for the user who asked.

definition.ja: ふだんは 1 つのリージョンだけがリクエストに答え、もう 1 つは切り替えに備えて待つ構成。両方が常に答える構成は active-active。
definition.en: A setup in which one Region answers requests and another waits to take over. When both always answer, it is active-active.

title.ja: Multi-Region: 2 つ目のリージョンが 1 か月に上乗せするもの（テーブル 1 GB、画像 10 GB）
title.en: Multi-Region: what the second Region adds in a month (1 GB table, 10 GB of images)

ja: 既定の 2 つのスタック。テーブルは各リージョンで 1 GB、point-in-time recovery は両方のレプリカで有効
書き込みは月 10 万回で、どれも 1 KB 以下。大阪のレプリカに同じ数の replicated write request unit がかかる。東京側の書き込みは、同じ単価の replicated write request unit に置き換わるので、上乗せには数えない
画像は 10 GB で、その写しを大阪に置く。月に 1 GB、10,000 個が新しく複製される。複製の PUT は大阪の通常の PUT の単価で計算
読み取り、Lambda、API Gateway、ログ、東京側の保存料は含めない。大阪の DynamoDB の保存料は、最初の 25 GB が USD 0 の段に入る
en: The two default stacks: a 1 GB table in each Region, with point-in-time recovery on both replicas

100,000 writes a month, each 1 KB or less. The Osaka replica is billed the same number of replicated write request units. Writes on the Tokyo side become replicated write request units at the same unit price, so they are not counted as added
10 GB of images with a copy in Osaka; 1 GB in 10,000 objects is newly replicated each month. Replication PUTs are computed at Osaka's ordinary PUT price
Reads, Lambda, API Gateway, logs, and storage on the Tokyo side are left out. DynamoDB storage in Osaka falls inside the first 25 GB, which is priced at USD 0

note.ja: 85 件。2 つのリージョンをメモリ上に置いたモデルで、MREC の複製の遅れ、2 つのリージョンからの同時の編集で片方が消えること、書き込みを 1 つのリージョンに寄せると 05章の検査が効くこと、カウンターの取りこぼし、東京を切り離したあとの上書きと遅れて届く書き込み、MRSC での 409 と孤立したリージョンの拒否。S3 の複製の規則（ルールより前のオブジェクト、削除マーカー、バージョン指定の削除、双方向、テーブルとの速さの差）。ヘルスチェックの判定、フェイルオーバーとレイテンシーの応答、古い DNS の答えを持つクライアント、RTO の内訳。リージョンごとの API の包み（ヘッダー、ヘルスチェック、書き込みの拒否）。スタックのアサーション。05章のリポジトリのコントラクトテストを、2 つのモードのレプリカに対して
note.en: 85 tests. On a model that keeps two Regions in memory: replication lag in MREC, one of two simultaneous edits from two Regions vanishing, chapter 05's check working again when writes go to one Region, a counter losing an increment, an overwrite after Tokyo is cut off and a write that arrives late, the 409 and the refusal of an isolated Region in MRSC. The rules of S3 replication (objects older than the rule, delete markers, deletes that name a version, two-way, the difference in speed from the table). Health check decisions, failover and latency answers, a client holding an old DNS answer, the parts of the RTO. The per-Region wrapper of the API (header, health check, refusing writes). Stack assertions. Chapter 05's repository contract against a replica in both modes

summary.ja: 28章の 2 つのスタックを AWS に一度もデプロイしていない。未確認: cdkd 0.296.28 が AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable（レプリカごとの PITR を含む）を作れること、ap-northeast-3 のスタックを同じアプリからデプロイできること（東京で bootstrap した状態で足りるか）、名前を固定した別リージョンのバケットへの複製の設定、`-c back=on` の 2 回目のデプロイ、ReplicationLatency の実際の値、2 つのリージョンから同時に編集したときにどちらが残るか。
summary.en: The two stacks of chapter 28 have never been deployed. Unconfirmed: that cdkd 0.296.28 can create the AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable (per-replica PITR included), that the ap-northeast-3 stack deploys from the same app (and whether a bootstrap done for Tokyo is enough), the replication configuration into a bucket in another Region referred to by a fixed name, the second deploy with `-c back=on`, real ReplicationLatency values, and which of two simultaneous edits from two Regions survives.

resume.ja: `vp run mr:standby:infra:deploy`、`vp run mr:infra:deploy` の順にデプロイし、`vp run mr:status` で両方のレプリカが ACTIVE であることを見る。`vp run mr:conflict --apply` の出力（2 つの PUT のステータスと、5 秒後に両方のリージョンが持つタイトル）を記録する。CloudWatch で ReplicationLatency を見る。最後に `vp run mr:empty --apply`、`vp run mr:infra:destroy`、`vp run mr:standby:infra:destroy`。
resume.en: Deploy with `vp run mr:standby:infra:deploy`, then `vp run mr:infra:deploy`, and check with `vp run mr:status` that both replicas are ACTIVE. Record what `vp run mr:conflict --apply` prints (the status of the two PUTs and the title both Regions hold five seconds later). Look at ReplicationLatency in CloudWatch. Finish with `vp run mr:empty --apply`, `vp run mr:infra:destroy`, and `vp run mr:standby:infra:destroy`.

summary.ja: リージョンの障害もフェイルオーバーも、一度も起こしていない。未確認: Route 53 のヘルスチェックが異常と判定するまでの実際の時間、API Gateway のカスタムドメインを指すエイリアスレコードの TTL、切り替わりにクライアントが気づくまでの時間、cdkd が AWS::Route53::HealthCheck・AWS::ApiGatewayV2::DomainName・ApiMapping を Cloud Control API 経由で作れること、2 つのスタックが同じドメインの ACM の証明書をそれぞれ DNS で検証できること、RTO と RPO の実測値。
summary.en: No Region failure and no failover was ever exercised. Unconfirmed: how long a Route 53 health check really takes to turn unhealthy, the TTL of an alias record that points to an API Gateway custom domain name, how long clients take to notice the switch, that cdkd can create AWS::Route53::HealthCheck, AWS::ApiGatewayV2::DomainName and ApiMapping through the Cloud Control API, that two stacks can each validate an ACM certificate for the same domain through DNS, and any measured RTO or RPO.

resume.ja: ホストゾーンを用意し、`-c domain=<name> -c zoneId=<id> -c zoneName=<zone>` を付けて 2 つのスタックをデプロイする。`dig <name>` で TTL を記録する。東京のスタックを `-c drill=on` でデプロイしてヘルスチェックを落とし、`x-aih-region` が ap-northeast-3 に変わるまでの時間を計って、`examples/28-multi-region/src/objectives.ts` の数字と比べる。AWS FIS のグローバルテーブルのアクションで複製を止める実験は、別に計画する。
resume.en: Prepare a hosted zone and deploy both stacks with `-c domain=<name> -c zoneId=<id> -c zoneName=<zone>`. Record the TTL that `dig <name>` shows. Deploy Tokyo's stack with `-c drill=on` so its health check fails, time how long `x-aih-region` takes to become ap-northeast-3, and compare it with the numbers in `examples/28-multi-region/src/objectives.ts`. Pausing replication with the AWS FIS global table actions is a separate experiment to plan.

summary.ja: MRSC のグローバルテーブルを、この章のスタックは作らない。固定した版の cdkd の GlobalTable の実装が扱うプロパティの一覧に MultiRegionConsistency と GlobalTableWitnesses がなく、3 つ目のリージョンも要るため。MRSC の動きはドキュメントとモデルだけで確かめた。孤立したリージョンで SDK が投げるエラーの名前は確認していない。
summary.en: This chapter's stacks do not create an MRSC global table: the list of properties handled by the pinned cdkd's GlobalTable provider has neither MultiRegionConsistency nor GlobalTableWitnesses, and a third Region is needed. MRSC behaviour was checked against the documentation and the model only. The name of the error the SDK throws in an isolated Region was not confirmed.

resume.ja: 空のテーブルを AWS CDK CLI か AWS CLI で MRSC（東京、大阪、ウィットネスにソウル）として作り、2 つのリージョンから同じ version への更新を同時に送って、ConditionalCheckFailedException と ReplicatedWriteConflictException のどちらが返るかを記録する。
resume.en: Create an empty table as MRSC (Tokyo, Osaka, witness in Seoul) with the AWS CDK CLI or the AWS CLI, send updates of the same version from two Regions at once, and record whether ConditionalCheckFailedException or ReplicatedWriteConflictException comes back.
